components.label: Client
components.responsibility: Own request identity and minimum observed write position.

components.label: Replicated storage boundary
components.responsibility: Expose the chosen acknowledgement and read guarantees.

components.label: Primary writer
components.responsibility: Serialize commands and durable receipts before acknowledging.

components.label: Durable write-ahead log
components.responsibility: Persist ordered commands and idempotency receipts.

components.label: Follower data store
components.responsibility: Replay durable entries and track applied position.

components.label: Replication sender
components.responsibility: Ship bounded batches and retry gaps from acknowledged offsets.

components.label: Read router
components.responsibility: Choose reads using declared consistency and session position.

components.label: Fenced leadership authority
components.responsibility: Allocate a unique writer epoch and fence the old primary through storage enforcement.

components.label: Consensus voter group
components.responsibility: Persist terms and votes and implement Raft voting/log matching/commit rules.

components.label: Commit-index gate
components.responsibility: Acknowledge current-term entries only after durable majority replication and commit advancement.

components.label: Snapshot coordinator
components.responsibility: Install a checked snapshot at a committed boundary, then replay its suffix.

components.label: Unified consistency router
components.responsibility: Reconcile leader discovery, session reads and command receipt handling.

components.label: Recovery log reader
components.responsibility: Fetch retained log suffixes or request a snapshot for lag beyond retention.

requirements.text: Specify exactly which failures an acknowledged write survives.
Expose read consistency and session progress explicitly.
Prevent an obsolete leader from accepting authoritative writes after failover.
Recover replicas without overwriting committed history; handle snapshot and log retention.

problem.scope: Compare asynchronous primary replication with a consensus-backed replicated log. The Raft branch names protocol obligations and uses a verified implementation in production; a majority-write sketch is not a complete consensus algorithm.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Async standby replication and acknowledgement durability differ.
references.title: PostgreSQL standby replication

references.supports: Leader election, log matching, commit rules, snapshots and membership obligations.
references.title: Raft paper

acceptanceCases.given: A write is acknowledged and the current primary permanently fails.
acceptanceCases.then: The async write can be absent; report the measured loss window rather than claiming zero loss.
acceptanceCases.when: Recover using a surviving follower group.

acceptanceCases.given: A write commits but its reply is lost.
acceptanceCases.then: Return the original receipt for the identical request; reject the changed payload.
acceptanceCases.when: Retry the same opId and then reuse it with a different value.

acceptanceCases.given: Caller observed position 12 but follower applied only 10.
acceptanceCases.then: Wait, route elsewhere, or return unavailable; never silently return position 10 as session-consistent.

acceptanceCases.given: Leader epoch T loses authority while isolated.
acceptanceCases.then: Storage fencing or consensus prevents old-authority acknowledgement.
acceptanceCases.when: A new leader is established and the old leader receives a write.

acceptanceCases.given: Follower is behind the oldest retained log record.
acceptanceCases.then: State equals replay from the committed history; inconsistent snapshot metadata is rejected.
acceptanceCases.when: Install snapshot S then replay the suffix.

guarantees: Reply guarantees are explicit; transport acknowledgements alone are insufficient.

assumptions: One writer; primary fsync is not remote durability.
Snapshots and operation receipts share the log recovery boundary.
solutions.chooseWhen: Low primary-write latency matters and the business accepts a nonzero recovery point.

invariants: Success means primary fsync; remote replication may lag.
stages.question: What does a successful write promise?
stages.reason: Start with the client and the storage abstraction.
stages.title: Declare the acknowledgement boundary

invariants: A returned operation receipt is persisted with its command.
stages.question: What survives a primary restart?
stages.reason: Expand the boundary into a writer and replayable command log.
stages.title: Separate writer and durable log

invariants: A received batch is not necessarily fsynced or applied.
stages.question: Which offset is durable and which is applied?
stages.reason: Separate transport acknowledgements from application progress.
stages.title: Add a separate follower

invariants: A session read waits, chooses a sufficiently caught-up node, or fails explicitly.
stages.question: Can a read observe the caller’s preceding write?
stages.reason: Add a read router with a minimum position watermark.
stages.title: Expose read consistency

invariants: An old epoch cannot append authoritative commands after fencing.
stages.question: How is an obsolete writer stopped?
stages.reason: Leadership needs an enforceable protocol, not a DNS update.
stages.title: Introduce an external fencing authority

invariants: Promotion reports its replayed position and the accepted loss window.
stages.question: Which writes can disappear after failover?
stages.reason: Tie reply visibility to the selected durability contract.
stages.title: Make promotion policy explicit

invariants: Verify hash and included index/term before replaying entries beyond the snapshot.
stages.question: What if lag exceeds retained log history?
stages.reason: Add a recovery boundary that never mixes unrelated snapshots and log suffixes.
stages.title: Install checked snapshots and replay suffixes

invariants: Duplicate requests return their original committed receipt or explicit uncertainty.

operations.reason: Join the session watermark and leader choice instead of keeping competing consistency decisions.

stages.question: Can discovery and read routing use conflicting leadership views?
stages.reason: One client consistency owner carries epoch, receipt and read watermark.
stages.title: Merge client consistency decisions

solutions.title: Asynchronous primary with explicit loss window
tradeoffs: A promoted async follower can lose previously acknowledged writes.
Safe failover requires fencing and an explicit choice of recovery position.
